deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1983-84 notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of n pseudolines in the real projective plane, including non-simple arrangements with multiple points.

(1) Top-left coloured figure. A pseudoline L (dark green) carries two multiple points: one of multiplicity ν (ν lines through it) and one of multiplicity ν'. L is the common line. The lines through at least one of the two points therefore number ν+ν'-1. The others number n-(ν+ν'-1) = (n-1)-(ν-1)-(ν'-1), which is the formula written at the top. The red lines show how the remaining lines pass through the strip around L between and beyond the two points. The labels n-ν, ν-1, (n-1)-(ν-1)-(ν'-1) count the lines crossing each side.

(2) Rectangles with tick marks. Top and bottom sides carry n-ν marks; the short sides carry ν-1 marks; the corners are black dots and an arrow orients the top. This is best read as the boundary of a tubular neighbourhood of a pseudoline L through a ν-fold point, cut open at that point. In P^2 that neighbourhood is a Möbius band whose boundary circle runs twice along L.
- Each of the n-ν lines not through the point crosses each 'sheet' once.
- The ν-1 other lines through the point cross the boundary near the point, at the two short sides.
- Total crossings: 2(n-ν)+2(ν-1) = 2(n-1), as it must be.
The variant with (ν-1)+1 on one side, and the lower rectangle with small squares at the corners and pencils fanning out, adapt this count when one of the lines is perturbed off the multiple point. The circled 2(ν-1) is the number of crossings contributed near the point.

(3) Top-right figure. A line moves across the multiple point (box a', a, b, b'): the green curve is pushed through the pencil of red lines. This is a local 'déformation' of the arrangement, a Ringel-type mutation generalised to a ν-fold point. The rectangle a, b, b', a' with red 'K' shapes and the star-plus-bracket pictures show the local strip before and after the move.

(4) Right-hand computations. Grothendieck is counting something attached to the configuration (crossings, edges or cells along the band) and trying several candidates in succession:
- 2n-(ν+ν'-2) (with the note 'ν+ν'-2 ≥ 2'),
- 2n-2(ν+ν'-1),
- 2n-(ν+ν'-1), which he settles on.
The partial counts n-ν, n-ν-(ν'-1), n-ν'+1, n-ν' are the pieces.

(5) Bottom. Four schematic pictures: a green arch (a portion of a pseudoline with marked points) over a horizontal chord, with brackets labelled ±1. In the last two pictures some labels are replaced by an unknown sign ε. He defines ε = +1 if 'la forme spéciale est du type sommital (ultra-spécial)', ε = -1 otherwise, and asks 'Comment trouver la valeur de ε ?'. This looks like a signed local contribution to an invariant (an Euler-characteristic-type or orientation/rotation count) for two types of 'special forms' in his own classification. The question is left open on this page.

In sum, the page counts lines and crossings around a line carrying two multiple points, for use in analysing deformations of non-simple arrangements, and ends on an undetermined sign.
errors: No outright error. Several trial formulas for the same count are written and struck or superseded (2n-(ν+ν'-2), 2n-2(ν+ν'-1)) before 2n-(ν+ν'-1); which quantity is being counted is not stated on the page.
The sign ε is left undetermined; the page's own closing question shows the computation is incomplete.

ideas.what: Counting lines through/not through two multiple points on a common pseudoline: n-(ν+ν'-1) = (n-1)-(ν-1)-(ν'-1)
ideas.modern_name: elementary incidence count in (non-simple) pseudoline arrangements

ideas.what: Boundary of the Möbius-band neighbourhood of a pseudoline as a closed curve crossing the arrangement 2(n-1) times, split as 2(n-ν)+2(ν-1) at a ν-fold point
ideas.modern_name: local/tubular neighbourhood of a pseudoline; zone of a line

ideas.what: Moving a pseudoline across a multiple point (local deformation)
ideas.modern_name: mutation/flip; Ringel's homotopy theorem, generalised to multiple points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel 1956; Goodman–Pollack; oriented matroid theory (Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler)

ideas.what: Sign ε attached to 'special forms' of 'sommital (ultra-special)' type versus others, entering a signed count
ideas.modern_name: unclear; possibly a local orientation/Euler-type contribution in a classification of degenerate configurations

missed.claim: Grothendieck introduces a sign ε distinguishing 'sommital (ultra-special)' special forms from others in a signed local count, and explicitly asks how to determine it. The question is unanswered on this page, and the terminology ('forme spéciale', 'sommital') belongs to his private classification of degenerate pseudoline configurations, which has not been published or analysed.
missed.quote: ε = +1 si la forme spéciale est du type sommital (ultra-spécial), −1 sinon. Comment trouver la valeur de ε ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If the surrounding pages make the classification and the invariant explicit, they could document an early, independent approach to the combinatorics of degenerations of pseudoline arrangements (related to the stratification of the realisation/oriented-matroid space). The page alone is too fragmentary to establish a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine incidence and crossing counts and local deformation pictures of the kind standard in pseudoline/oriented-matroid combinatorics. The only non-routine element is the open question about the sign ε for 'sommital' special forms, which relies on undefined private terminology and cannot be assessed from this page alone.
transcription_corrections: Top formula: the struck symbol in '(n-1)[-+-](ν-1)' is a crossed-out character; the intended identity is n-(ν+ν'-1) = (n-1)-(ν-1)-(ν'-1).
The circled '2(ν-1)' is a separate annotation in the left middle of the page, not part of the a', a, b, b' labels.
The ε definition reads 'si la forme spéciale est du type sommital (ultra-spécial)'; the struck word after 'ultra' appears to be 'spécial'.
The labels '(ν-1)' and '(ν-1)+1' belong to the short sides of the small top-right rectangle, whose long sides are labelled n-ν.
